chunks.text:
Losartan is used alone or in combination with other medications to treat high blood pressure in adults and children at least 6 years old.
Losartan is also used to decrease the risk of stroke.
This use applies to people who have high blood pressure.
It also applies to people with a heart condition called left ventricular hypertrophy.
Left ventricular hypertrophy is the enlargement of the walls of the left side of the heart.
Losartan may not decrease the risk of stroke in African Americans who have these conditions.
Losartan is also used to treat kidney disease.
This treatment is for people who have type 2 diabetes.
Type 2 diabetes is a condition in which the body does not use insulin normally.
Consequently, the body cannot control the amount of sugar in the blood.
Losartan is also used to treat high blood pressure.
Losartan belongs to a class of medications called angiotensin II receptor antagonists.
Losartan works by blocking the action of certain natural substances.
These substances tighten the blood vessels.
Blocking them allows the blood to flow more smoothly.

Tell your doctor right away if you become pregnant.
Losartan can cause injury or death to the unborn baby.
If you have diabetes, do not use losartan together with any medication that contains aliskiren.
Aliskiren is a blood pressure medicine.
You may also need to avoid taking losartan with aliskiren if you have kidney disease.
In rare cases, losartan can cause a condition.
The condition results in the breakdown of skeletal muscle tissue.
The breakdown leads to kidney failure.
Call your doctor right away if you have unexplained muscle pain.
Call your doctor right away if you have muscle tenderness.
Call your doctor right away if you have muscle weakness.
Call your doctor right away if you have a fever.
Call your doctor right away if you have unusual tiredness.
Call your doctor right away if you have dark colored urine.

chunks.text:
You should not use losartan if you are allergic to losartan.
If you have diabetes, do not take losartan with any medication that contains aliskiren.
Aliskiren is a blood pressure medicine.
To make sure losartan is safe for you, tell your doctor if you have ever had:
heart disease or congestive heart failure;
an electrolyte imbalance (such as high levels of potassium in your blood);
if you are on a low-salt diet;
liver disease; or
kidney disease.
You may also need to avoid taking losartan with aliskiren if you have kidney disease.
Stop using losartan and tell your doctor right away if you become pregnant.
Losartan can cause injury or death to the unborn baby.
You should not breastfeed while using losartan and for 2 days after your last dose.

chunks.text:
Take losartan exactly as prescribed by your doctor.
Follow all directions on your prescription label and read all medication guides or instruction sheets.
Your doctor may occasionally change your dose.
Losartan is usually taken once per day.
You may take losartan with or without food.
Call your doctor if you are sick with vomiting or diarrhea, or if you are sweating more than usual.
You can easily become dehydrated while taking losartan.
Dehydrated can lead to very low blood pressure, a serious electrolyte imbalance, or kidney failure.
Your blood pressure will need to be checked often.
You may need frequent blood tests.
If you have high blood pressure, keep using Losartan even if you feel well.
High blood pressure often has no symptoms.
Store tightly closed at room temperature, away from moisture, heat, and light.

chunks.text:
Usual Adult Dose for Diabetic Nephropathy:
The initial dose is 50 mg orally once a day.
The maximum dose is 100 mg orally once a day.
If hypertensive patients with left ventricular hypertrophy require titration from the initial dose, increase to 100 mg orally once a day.
If type 2 diabetic nephropathy patients require titration from the initial dose, increase to 100 mg orally once a day.
Antihypertension is substantially present within 1 week.
In some studies, the maximal effect occurred in 3 to 6 weeks.
Uses: -Treatment of hypertension.
-To reduce the risk of stroke in patients with hypertension and left ventricular hypertrophy.
-Treatment of diabetic nephropathy with an elevated serum creatinine and proteinuria (urinary albumin to creatinine ratio 300 mg/g or greater) in patients with type 2 diabetes and a history of hypertension.
Usual Adult Dose for Hypertension:
The initial dose is 50 mg orally once a day.
The maximum dose is 100 mg orally once a day.

chunks.section_heading: What happens if I miss a dose?
chunks.text:
Take Losartan as soon as you can.

chunks.text:

Do not use potassium supplements or salt substitutes, unless your doctor has told you to.

chunks.text:
Get emergency medical help if you have signs of an allergic reaction to losartan.
These signs include hives, difficulty breathing, and swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat.
Losartan may cause serious side effects.
Call your doctor at once if you have:
a light-headed feeling, like you might pass out;
high blood potassium - nausea, weakness, tingly feeling, chest pain, irregular heartbeats, loss of movement; or
kidney problems - swelling, urinating less, feeling tired or short of breath.
Common losartan side effects may include:
dizziness, tiredness;
low blood pressure;
low blood sugar;
diarrhea;
back pain; or
cold symptoms such as stuffy nose, sneezing, sore throat.
This is not a complete list of side effects and others may occur.
Call your doctor for medical advice about side effects.
You may report side effects to FDA at 1-800-FDA-1088.

chunks.section_heading: What other drugs will affect losartan?
chunks.text:
Sometimes it is not safe to use certain medicines at the same time.
Some drugs can affect your blood levels of other drugs you use.
This may increase side effects.
This may make the medicines less effective.
Tell your doctor about all your other medicines, especially:
a diuretic or "water pill" that may increase blood potassium such as spironolactone, triamterene, amiloride;
NSAIDs (nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs) - aspirin, ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin), naproxen (Aleve), celecoxib, diclofenac, indomethacin, meloxicam, and others; or
heart or blood pressure medication.
lithium.
This list is not complete.
Other drugs may affect losartan.
These other drugs include prescription and over-the-counter medicines.
These other drugs also include vitamins and herbal products.
Not all possible drug interactions are listed here.
